caveats: This is mostly high fashion as written up in books, encyclopaedias and museums, not what everyone wore.
Museums collect couture, famous designers and whatever happened to survive, so their counts show what got collected, not how popular something was.
Museum collections thin out after 2000, so a drop in recent museum counts is about collecting, not fashion.
Books trail clothes: the Ngram curves often peak years after a look was in the shops, and some phrases also mean other things, so compare the shape of a curve, not its height.
Ngram data ends in 2022, so the newest micro trends have no curve.
Runway counts start in 1988, are thin before 2000, and leave out years with fewer than 100 looks. They are shares of looks with an automatic image tag, and tagging changed over the years too.
Museum dates pile up on round years, because objects dated to a decade get its first year. Group by decade before reading too much into a single year.
The scope is Western fashion: the UK, the US, France and Italy, plus looks not tied to one place.
A few trend periods and revival originals start before 1920. Clamp them to the timeline if needed.
Revivals with a null trend are era-wide comebacks such as 1970s styles; the subject field says what came back.

Other sportswear trends included tracksuits, tunic shirts, crop tops, tube tops, sweatshirts, hip-huggers, low rise pants, and leisure suits.
Other trends included wedge flip flops, hot pants, denim jackets, chunky sweaters, pashmina scarves, Skechers footwear, crop tops, and tube tops.

trends.description: Wide shorts or trousers cut to look like a skirt.
trends.name: Culottes

sources.quote: In April 1931, Spanish player Lili de Álvarez caused a sensation at Wimbledon by appearing in divided skirts of Schiaparelli's design, while two years later Alice Marble appeared in shorts above the knee.

For clients who had to cycle because of petrol rationing, Piguet and Balenciaga designed culottes to be worn hidden beneath skirts; Hermès offered zippered belts to conceal valuables and shoulder bags resembling hunting pouches.
Examples included the miniskirt, culottes, go-go boots, alongside more experimental designs made from synthetic materials such as polyvinyl chloride (PVC).

trends.description: A fringe parted in the middle and swept to each side.
trends.name: Curtain bangs

sources.quote: By 2019, curtain bangs began to trend, often paired with layered cuts reminiscent of 90s styles.

Popular styles included curtain bangs, permed hair (referred to as the "broccoli haircut" by Generation Z), the "wet mop," mullets (particularly in the US and Australia), the "Edgar cut," and shaggy hair.

Popular styles included curtain bangs, 1980s, 1990s and early 2000s-inspired bangs, hair extensions, ponytails, twin pigtails, French braid, shaggy hair commonly known as the "wolf cut", and natural hair for Black American women.

trends.description: Hair parted in the middle and falling either side of the face.
trends.name: Curtains haircut

sources.quote: More rebellious young men went for longer, unkempt "grunge" hair, often with a center part.
By the end of the decade, sleek, bone-straight hair regained dominance, often styled with center parts and a “glass” finish.
For boys, short haircuts such as the quiff, the buzzcut, curtains, crew cut, and Caesar cut were popular in the early 2000s till mid 2000s.

trends.description: Tweed, knitwear and old-university gloom.
trends.name: Dark academia

sources.quote: Cottagecore was first named on Tumblr in 2018 and is related to similar internet aesthetics including goblincore and dark academia.

The dark academia or old money aesthetic of the early to mid 2020s, which combined elements of preppy fashion and gothic fashion, was heavily influenced by 1930s and 1940s fashion, particularly attire worn by students at Oxbridge, Ivy League colleges, and prep schools during the time.

A closely related style, known as "light academia", was characterized by neutral and light colors, including soft blues, pinks, whites, creamy yellows, beige, light greys, light purple, pastel and dusty colors, plaid, stripes, and argyle patterns reminiscent of the preppy look of the early 1980s.

trends.description: Lipstick in black, brown, plum or deep wine.
trends.name: Dark lipstick

sources.quote: Barbara Stanwyck embodied the look with sharp-shouldered suits, dark lipstick, and lacquered blonde hair.
It became more and more common to see not only black clothes but also stark black eyeliner, hair dyed black, black nail polish, and even black lipstick, on both sexes.

Gothic makeup had broken into the mainstream, having been made up of vamp lipstick (or even black lipstick), heavy mascara and eyeliner, often purple-tinted eye shadow (or else very dark blue), and extremely pale foundation.

trends.description: A loose, brightly patterned West African tunic worn as a statement of Black pride.
trends.name: Dashiki

sources.quote: At the same time, some aspects of traditional attire such as wooden jewelry or the Dashiki were worn by expatriate Africans in the West, African Americans, and some liberal white Americans.

Hippies often chose brightly colored clothing and wore unusual styles, such as bell-bottom pants, vests, tie-dyed garments, dashikis, peasant blouses, and long, full skirts; non-Western inspired clothing with Native American, Latin American, African and Asiatic motifs was also popular.

Typical clothing included black leather jackets, vests, black driving gloves, leather peaked caps embellished with chains and metal studs, African folk costume like the fez or dashiki, traditional African colors like black, red, yellow or green, Ancient Egyptian jewelry such as the Ankh, gold chains, and railroad stripe pants for women.

trends.description: Clothes shown unfinished, asymmetric or inside out.
trends.name: Deconstruction

sources.quote: Elements of deconstruction in costume became an important element of commercial fashion.

Yamamoto, Kawakubo and Miyake redefined the concepts of deconstruction and minimalism that were used in fashion design worldwide by pioneering monochromatic, androgynous, asymmetrical, and baggy looks.

This was a loosening and increase in scale of the popular, casual peasant styles of the late sixties and early seventies and a reduction and elimination of internal structure like linings and padding to achieve what was known as an unconstructed look and feel.

trends.description: Indigo cotton twill, from workwear to everything.
trends.name: Denim

sources.quote: Denim became increasingly common in a wider range of settings, including casual and formal occasions.
Denim's popularity was at an all-time high in Europe, with designer denim jackets and matching jeans rocketing in prices.
The popularity of jeans led to blue denim being used for many other garments, as well as other fabrics being given a blue denim look.

trends.description: A jean jacket, often customised with patches.
trends.name: Denim jacket

sources.quote: By the late 1980s, acid-washed jeans and denim jackets had become popular with both sexes.
Denim jackets, neon-colored windbreakers and other brightly colored outerwear reflected an interest in 1980s styles.
Denim's popularity was at an all-time high in Europe, with designer denim jackets and matching jeans rocketing in prices.

trends.description: Jeans cut off above the knee.
trends.name: Denim cut-offs

sources.quote: Other trends included whale tails, cargo pants, and hip-hop inspired sweatpants, denim shorts, and brightly colored tights.
Both men and women wore their shorts at the upper thigh, with cut-off blue-jean shorts extremely popular, usually worn with t-shirts or tank tops.

Due to its association with rappers, sportswear became acceptable to wear in public throughout the mid- to late 1990s, especially oversized T-shirts, baseball caps and sweaters bearing the New York Yankees logo, tennis shoes, hoodies, jean shorts, khaki cargo pants, baggy basketball shorts, chinos, tracksuits and black bomber jackets with orange linings.

trends.description: Suede ankle boots on a crepe sole.
trends.name: Desert boots

sources.quote: Desirable accessories during the mid-1990s included loafers, desert boots, chelsea boots, gold jewellery, boat shoes, chunky digital watches, solid colored ties, shoulder bags, and black/neon colored high-top sneakers replaced combat boots.

Male mods adopted a smooth, sophisticated look that included tailor-made suits with narrow lapels (sometimes made of mohair), skinny ties, button-down collar shirts, wool or cashmere jumpers (crewneck or V-neck), Chelsea or Beatle boots, loafers, Clarks desert boots, bowling shoes, and hairstyles that imitated the look of French Nouvelle Vague film actors.

Common footwear included classic Air Jordan sneakers, loafers with chunky brothel creeper soles, suede desert boots, Vans sneakers, imitation leather Adidas trainers, suede Timberland boots, Gucci loafers, duck boots, suede Beatle boots, chunky hiking sandals, high top Converse All-Stars, Nike Air Max sneakers, worker boots, and combat boots bought as army surplus.

trends.description: Expensive jeans with a famous name on the back pocket.
trends.name: Designer jeans

sources.quote: In 1978, the first designer jeans were introduced and immediately became popular, designers like Calvin Klein, Gloria Vanderbilt, and Fiorucci advertising their name on the back of the fashionable cigarette-leg, usually dark blue denim jean of the time.

Widespread fashions for women in the early 1980s included sweaters (including turtleneck, crew neck, and v-neck varieties); fur-lined puffer jackets; tunics; faux-fur coats; velvet blazers; trench coats (made in both fake and real leather); crop tops; tube tops; knee-length skirts (of no prescribed length, as designers opted for choice); loose, flowy, knee-length dresses (with high-cut and low-cut necklines, varying sleeve lengths, and made in a variety of fabrics including cotton, silk, satin, and polyester); high-waisted loose pants; embroidered jeans; leather pants; and designer jeans, though jeans were not as widely worn as during the 1970s.
Certain designer produces became highlight sought after during the early and middle years of the 200s.

trends.description: Glowing, glassy, hydrated-looking skin.
trends.name: Dewy skin

sources.quote: One of the most talked-about trends in skincare was "slugging," where people applied a thick layer of petroleum jelly on their face to keep moisture in and protect their skin.
Several other more short-lived trends were born out of this, such as strobing in 2015 and 2016 which consisted of using glowy highlighters to accentuate the high points of the face.
Also around the second half of the decade, there was an increasing amount of emphasis on the perfection of complexions, with illuminators and shimmer products becoming must-have items.

trends.description: Shiny, stretchy clubwear for the dance floor.
trends.name: Disco

sources.quote: The disco music genre spawned its own fashion craze in the mid- to late 1970s.
From 1997 onwards, many British and American designers started to take cues from the disco fashion of the mid–late 1970s.
Disco fashions were very trendy in the late 1970s.

trends.description: Air-cushioned leather work boots taken up by skinheads, punks and grunge.
trends.name: Doc Martens

sources.quote: Doc Martens were dark shoes or boots with air-cushioned soles that were worn by both sexes in the 1980s.

The early skinheads retained basic elements of mod fashion—such as Fred Perry and Ben Sherman shirts, Sta-Prest trousers and Levi's jeans—but mixed them with working class-orientated accessories such as braces and Dr. Martens work boots.

In a 1998 article for the Journal of Cultural Geography, Thomas Bell said "Flannel shirts and Doc Martens boots were worn as an anti-fashion statement that is undoubtedly related to the unassuming and unvarnished nature of the music itself".

trends.description: A studded leather collar worn as a punk necklace.
trends.name: Dog collar

sources.quote: Women's hippie accessories of the early 1970s included chokers, dog collars, handcrafted neck ornaments, and accessories made from natural elements like wood, shells, stones, feathers, Indian beads and leather.

Notable necklaces of the time were long pearl or beaded necklaces, Dog collar necklaces (similar to a choker, but worn lower), drop earrings, and large bracelets (typically made of thick or thin wood, bone, shell, metal, or plastic - sometimes with gems, often mimicking African tribal art).

They were an important feature of the post-punk 1980s Gothic look which featured long, back-combed hair, pale skin, dark eyeshadow, eyeliner, and lipstick, black nail varnish, spiked bracelets and dog-collars, black clothing (often made of gabardine), and leather or velvet trimmed in lace or fishnet material.

trends.description: Bright, joyful colour to lift the mood.
trends.name: Dopamine dressing

sources.quote: This "dopamine dressing" movement featured long skirts, belted maxi dresses with thigh splits, and plenty of gold and pearl jewelry, along with neon blue tights.
These chunky pieces echoed 1980s power dressing and 1950s costume jewelry, contributing to the overall look of retro maximalism.
As the decade began, maximalist fashion resurfaced on the runway to express individuality and break away from the previous decades minimalist style.

trends.description: A suit jacket with overlapping fronts and two columns of buttons.
trends.name: Double-breasted suit

sources.quote: A British wartime phenomenon was the "spiv" or "wide boy"—a black market street trader recognizable by his double-breasted suit, soft hat worn at a rakish angle, wide tie, and neatly trimmed mustache.

After years in wartime uniform, men returned to civilian dress with what Esquire called the "Bold Look" in October 1948—broad-shouldered jackets, long-roll lapels, and predominantly double-breasted suits.
Double-breasted blazers inspired by 1940s styles returned as power suits in the 1980s.

trends.description: Denim on top and bottom at once.
trends.name: Double denim

sources.quote: Cowboy boots, elaborately embroidered western shirts with pearl snaps inspired by Nudie Cohn's bespoke pieces, bolo ties, Stetsons, double denim "Texan tuxedos", jean jackets, and blue jeans were popular among both sexes.
Vintage clothing, khaki chinos, workmen's clothes, sweatshirts, leather coats, and all-denim outfits were also desired among young men.

A denim emphasis continued from the early seventies, particularly strong in 1973 to '75, with denim and denim-look fabrics of various intensities of indigo paired with blue jeans, usually flared, and denim skirts in below-knee lengths.

trends.description: A long, loose jacket with a velvet collar, the Teddy Boy signature.
trends.name: Drape jacket

sources.quote: Brothel creepers, drainpipe trousers, bolo ties and drape jackets were popular, typically with contrasting velvet collars and cuffs.

The new generation of Teds adopted some aspects of the 1950s but with a large glam rock influence, including louder colours for drape jackets, brothel creepers, and socks and shiny satin shirts worn with bootlace ties, jeans and big-buckled belts.
This style came to be known as the "English drape" and was promoted by Savile Row tailors Anderson & Sheppard.

trends.description: Hair matted and twisted into ropes.
trends.name: Dreadlocks

sources.quote: The skaters (nicknamed grebos or moshers) had long hair or dreadlocks and wore grunge inspired padded flannel overshirts and baggy pants as these were less likely to rip when skateboarding.
Clothing tends to be unsanitary by conventional standards, and dreadlocks are popular.
Also gaudy coloured hair, dreadlocks, tattoos and piercings came into fashion with ravers.

trends.description: A waistline that sits at the hips.
trends.name: Dropped waist

sources.quote: Day dresses had a drop waist, which was a belt around the low waist or hip and a skirt that hung anywhere from the ankle on up to the knee, never above.

Balenciaga had already introduced an unfitted suit jacket in 1951 and showed an unfitted dress by 1954; Dior presented his A line in 1955; and by 1957 the "sack" (or "bag") dress—combining a loose body with a dropped waist that recalled the silhouettes of the 1920s, typically worn with an updated version of the cloche hat—had been launched by multiple designers.

Crolla's giant cabbage rose prints, modeled after old chintz drapery fabric and needlework, seemed ubiquitous in 1984 and '85, initially shown by the designer on sixties-revival Nehru jackets and avant-garde UK street silhouettes like oversized sweaters and ankle-length tube skirts but soon picked up by Jean-Paul Gaultier in Paris and, before long, mass-marketed everywhere, especially popular in drop-waist, bertha-collared, puff-sleeved dresses to the lower calf put out by companies like Laura Ashley and worn with matching large hair bows on the back of the head.

trends.description: Hair dyed vivid, unnatural colours.
trends.name: Brightly dyed hair

sources.quote: Along with these hairstyles, 1960s-inspired beehive hairdos were popularized by British pop singers Emily Capell and Joy Crookes Early 2000s fashion-inspired straightened and brightly dyed hair was made popular by Doja Cat and Billie Eilish from 2021 to 2022.
This two-tone look was sometimes referred to as "e-girl streaks" and was associated with the rising influence of TikTok.
Also gaudy coloured hair, dreadlocks, tattoos and piercings came into fashion with ravers.

trends.description: TikTok-era emo revival with chains, striped tops and painted hearts.
trends.name: E-girls and e-boys

sources.quote: The pop-punk revival of early 2020s saw artists like Machine Gun Kelly and Yungblud influenced by the e-boy look, blending alterative fashion with their music.
In the late 2010s, a softer, goth inspired, style of makeup came into fashion, this was called egirl makeup.
E-kids' fashion is described as being inspired by skater culture, 1990s fashion, anime, hip-hop, kpop, emo rap, and trap metal.

trends.description: Browns, rusts and mustards.
trends.name: Earth tones

sources.quote: Color palettes instead favored earth tones and muted pastels, such as blush pink, camel, olive, mauve, and various shades of gray.

Key garments included oversized linen gilets, cotton twill maxi skirts, pinafore dresses, cropped dungaree pants with multiple pockets, chunky knitted cardigan sweaters, and earth tones such as olive green, brown, sage green, marigold yellow, tangerine orange, and ecru.
Rust, tangerine, copper, forest green, and pistachio became more popularized from 1973 onwards.

trends.description: Rhinestoned T-shirts and caps printed with tattoo art.
trends.name: Ed Hardy

sources.quote: This trend, popularised by models like Dita Von Teese, gave rise to the popularity among all sexes of Ed Hardy clothing which lasted from 2007 until 2012.
Visual motifs such as tattoo designs, rhinestones, and emo inspired imagery remained popular, as well as brands like Juicy Couture, Von Dutch, and Ed Hardy.
Brands like Ed Hardy, Hot Topic, and Affliction, which were popular in the late 2000s, made a return, integrating past fashion trends with contemporary preferences.

trends.description: Black skinny jeans, band tees and side fringes.
trends.name: Emo

sources.quote: These included emo, indie, scene, psychobilly, preppy, skater, goth, nu metal, raver culturesrs, as well as hip-hop.

trends.description: A waistline raised to just under the bust.
trends.name: Empire line

sources.quote: Bridgerton inspired and popularized empire-line, linen milkmaid dresses, as well as maxi dresses.
Empire-waist shirts were also worn with belts.
Blouses and dresses were often cut in the empire or babydoll line, and were cinched at the waist with a wide-belt.

trends.description: A very short, slicked boyish cut for women.
trends.name: Eton crop

sources.quote: Boyish cuts were in vogue and released the weight of the tradition of women being required to grow their hair long, through popular cuts such as the bob cut, Eton crop, and shingle bob.
A more masculine look became popular, including flattened breasts and hips, short hairstyles such as the bob cut, Eton crop, and the Marcel wave.

The androgynous style popular among women in the 1920s, characterized by short, cropped hair, gave way in the 1930s to longer locks that were increasingly styled in elegant updos as the decade progressed.

trends.description: Bands of colourful knitted motifs from Shetland.
trends.name: Fair Isle

sources.quote: Tan gabardine trench coats, preppy Aran and Fair Isle cardigans, and safari suits were in demand for business casual wear.

The Fair Isle sweater, previously confined to sportswear, was widely adopted as casual wear under his influence; plus fours began to be worn off the golf course; and his other signatures—tweed sports jackets, low two-tone or suede shoes, chalk-striped fabrics, and belts rather than suspenders—were extensively imitated.

Brown replaced black as the most popular color for leather jackets, and common accessories included orange hoodies, black track pants, faded jeans covered in iron-on patches, black or white leather hi-tops, Timberland boots, navy blue wool coach jackets, graphic print tees featuring a small statement design, dark flannel sportcoats, cambric shackets, or camouflage jackets layered over cardigans or Alpine patterned sweaters, and white Adidas sneakers.

trends.description: Long, thick lashes, glued on or extended.
trends.name: False eyelashes

sources.quote: In the late 2000s, there was a craze for fake eyelashes, started by Lady Gaga.
Dark mascara, false eyelashes, dyed hair and cheek blush were popularised by Instagram social media influencers in the UK, American and Dubai such as Olivia Buckland and Huda Kattan.
False eyelashes were in vogue, as was pale lipstick.

trends.description: A small zipped pouch worn on a belt around the waist.
trends.name: Bum bag

sources.quote: The fanny pack accessory made a late comeback in 2018 with new packs introduced by fashion designers Gucci, Prada, and Louis Vuitton.

Common accessories include Ray-Ban wayfarer sunglasses, paisley scarfs, teashade glasses, tortoise shell glasses, snake skin or plaited leather belts, flat caps, newsboy caps, bum bags, trilbys, and pork pie hats.

trends.description: Synthetic fur, often in bright colours or animal prints.
trends.name: Faux fur

sources.quote: In this show models were wearing sheath-like dresses made of loosely knitted yarn and denim jackets with large fake fur collars.
For daytime outerwear, vinyl raincoats, colorful swing coats, bubble dresses, helmet-like hats, and dyed fake furs were popular for young women.

Shimmery jumpsuits, knitted dresses, and leather pilot jackets with faux fur collars added flair, while bold vertical-striped skirts, bootcut trouser suits, and jeans with glittery accents completed the look.

trends.description: A long fluffy scarf of feathers.
trends.name: Feather boa

sources.quote: Men on the red carpet are wearing more accessories, like feather boas and pearl jewelry.They are also choosing popular clothing items such as kimono-style shirts, frilly lace blouses, and tunics.
Feather boas were occasionally worn.
Widespread accessories included wristbands and collars, whistles, pacifiers, feather boas, cyberpunk inspired goggles, glow sticks, and record bags made of truck tarpaulins.

trends.description: Hair cut in layers and blow-dried back like wings, Farrah Fawcett style.
trends.name: Feathered hair

sources.quote: The early 2000s also continued the Farrah Fawcett hairstyle revival of the late 1990s.
The Farrah Fawcett hairstyle made a comeback, with highlights going hand-in-hand with this revival.

Other hairstyles of the early to mid-1970s included the wavy "gypsy" cut, the layered shag, and the "flicked" style, popularly referred to as "wings", in which the hair was flicked into resembling small wings at the temples.

trends.description: A soft felt hat with a pinched crown.
trends.name: Fedora

sources.quote: The fedora and the homburg—revived when President Eisenhower wore one to his inauguration in 1952 rather than the customary top hat—were the most fashionable styles, with brims generally narrower than in previous decades.
Middle-class men wore either a fedora, bowler hat, or a trilby hat.

Hats—exempt from coupon rationing—received more creative attention than almost any other garment; shapes ranged from Arab-style pillboxes to fedoras to pointed stocking caps, and milliners made imaginative use of whatever materials were available.

trends.description: Short hair set in S-shaped waves close to the head.
trends.name: Finger waves

sources.quote: A more masculine look became popular, including flattened breasts and hips, short hairstyles such as the bob cut, Eton crop, and the Marcel wave.
The predominant style in the early 1930s consisted of short hair styled with soft waves.
Hair was worn in numerous variations of softly waved styles.

trends.description: Gloves with the fingertips cut off, often lace.
trends.name: Fingerless gloves

sources.quote: In her album "Like a Virgin" phase, millions of young girls around the world emulated her fashion example that included brassieres worn as outerwear, huge crucifix jewelry, lace gloves, tulle skirts, and boytoy belts.

Men also wore acid wash jeans, patterned wool sweaters with turtlenecks underneath, black Schott Perfecto leather jackets, sheepskin coats, olive green anoraks, corduroy sportcoats, grey sweatpants and fingerless gloves.

Popular clothing included No Fear T-shirts, webbing belts, army surplus patrol caps, band T-shirts, dog tags, shark tooth necklaces, camouflage cargo pants, carpenter jeans, tuques, and fingerless gloves in dark colors like black, olive drab, burgundy, and navy blue.

trends.description: Open-mesh tights or stockings, a burlesque staple that punks took up.
trends.name: Fishnets

sources.quote: Some skingirls wore fishnet stockings and mini-skirts, a style introduced during the punk-influenced skinhead revival.
Gloves (sometimes laced or fingerless) were popularized by Madonna, as well as fishnet stockings and layers of beaded necklaces.

In the late 2000s, the soft grunge fashion style and Internet aesthetic evolved directly from the indie sleaze trend, once Tumblr users began to merge it with darker fashion elements like fishnets, chokers and combat boots.

trends.description: A soft checked work shirt, the uniform of grunge.
trends.name: Flannel shirt

sources.quote: Some punks bought T-shirts or plaid flannel shirts and wrote political slogans, band names or other punk-related phrases on them with marker pens.
By the mid-1990s the grunge style had gone mainstream in Britain and the US, and was dominated by tartan flannel shirts and stonewashed blue jeans.

In a 1998 article for the Journal of Cultural Geography, Thomas Bell said "Flannel shirts and Doc Martens boots were worn as an anti-fashion statement that is undoubtedly related to the unassuming and unvarnished nature of the music itself".

trends.description: Young 1920s women who cut their hair, raised their hems, wore loose dresses and partied.
trends.name: Flappers

sources.quote: The flapper dress was functional and flattened the bust line rather than accentuating it.
Flapper dresses were straight and loose, leaving the arms bare (sometimes no straps at all) and dropping the waistline to the hips.
The most memorable fashion trend of the Roaring Twenties was undoubtedly "the flapper" look.

trends.description: A rounded cloth cap with a small stiff brim.
trends.name: Flat cap

sources.quote: Working-class men wore a standard newsboy cap or a flat cap.
Common accessories included cashmere wool scarfs in neutral tones like white or ecru, loafers, chelsea boots and flat caps inspired by Peaky Blinders.
Hats common among skinheads include: Trilby hats; pork pie hats; flat caps (Scally caps or driver caps), winter woollen hats (without a bobble).

trends.description: A soft synthetic pile jacket from outdoor gear.
trends.name: Fleece jacket

sources.quote: Winter clothing included hiking jackets, fleeces, puffer jackets, padded flannel shirts, and turtleneck sweaters.

Popular accessories include horn rimmed glasses, high waisted pants especially pleated khaki chinos, dad hats, zip up polar fleeces, white or blue button down shirts, socks with sandals, turtlenecks, white tennis shoes, pocket protectors, leather shoes, plain sweaters in muted colors, and, for women, "mom jeans".

By 2001, popular mainstream trends included tight shirts, bell bottoms, platform shoes, fleeces, cropped tank tops, Union Jack motifs inspired by the Cool Britannia movement, and military inspired clothing, such as flak jackets with camouflage patterns.

trends.description: Printed flowers, from ditsy to oversized.
trends.name: Floral print

sources.quote: Sales in floral print clothing designs for men more than doubled amongst fashion retailers between 2013 and 2014.

The most internationally recognizable styles to come out of the London milieu were probably the large, tapestry-like floral prints from Crolla and the oversized "message shirts" with large block lettering from Katharine Hamnett.
Key items include oversized sweaters, cardigans, loose blouses, long skirts, floral dresses, and overalls.

trends.description: Flowers as hippie symbols, painted, printed and worn in the hair.
trends.name: Flower power

sources.quote: Hosiery manufacturers of the time like Mary Quant (who founded Pamela Mann Legwear) combined the "Flower Power" style of dress and the Pop Art school of design to create fashion tights that would appeal to a female audience that enjoyed psychedelia.
Other trends connected to the show included high-heeled shoes, designer handbags, large fabric flowers, and berets.

Typically middle class youths from Britain, America and New Zealand, these practitioners of free love favored a unisex look with long hair, tie dye and flower power motifs, Bob Dylan caps, kurtas, hemp waistcoats, baja jackets, bell bottoms, sandals, and maxi skirts for the girls.

trends.description: Football fans in expensive sportswear labels instead of team colours.
trends.name: Football casuals

sources.quote: The football casual subculture first appeared in the UK around 1983, when many ex-skinheads began dressing in designer clothing and sportswear to blend into the crowd and avoid police attention at football games.

trends.description: Hanging tassels of fabric or leather.
trends.name: Fringe

sources.quote: In addition, decorative embellishments on dresses such as fringe threads swung and jingled in sync with the movement of the body.
Alternatively, some went for an opposite feel with sequined tuxedo jackets or a more "western" look with western shirts or fringe jackets.

Movies and television exerted a powerful influence on children's play clothes: The Roy Rogers Show and the Davy Crockett craze inspired cowboy and frontier-style fringed pullovers, sueded fabrics, and the famous "coonskin" cap; Flash Gordon encouraged a Space Age look.

trends.description: Spiky hair with the ends bleached blond.
trends.name: Frosted tips

sources.quote: A common haircut among American men and boys was the frosted spiky hair popularized by boybands and pop punk bands from 1997 through 2004, 2005–2008.
Blonde-streaked or "frosted" hair was also popular.

trends.description: A wide skirt cut from a full circle, like the 1950s poodle skirt, often held out by petticoats.
trends.name: Full skirt

sources.quote: The style gained further currency when Princess Elizabeth wore a felt circle skirt with appliqué decoration on an official visit to Canada, encouraging its widespread adoption among teenage girls.
Later, they adopted the American fashions of toreador trousers, voluminous circle skirts, and hair in ponytails.
Working from the romantic styles of the late 1930s, designers offered dresses with defined waists and full skirts and sleeves; waists grew smaller, hips larger, and drapery was common.

trends.description: A coat, stole or trim of real fur.
trends.name: Fur coat

sources.quote: Fur coats returned to fashion, while some consumers chose alternative materials in response to concerns about animal cruelty.
Mink and sealskin were especially popular for fur coats, while cloth coats often featured fur cuffs and collars of mink, leopard, or Persian lamb.
Fur was a dominant feature of the era's outerwear: mink had become the ultimate status symbol, while sable and fox were also prized.

trends.description: A flat-chested, straight, boyish line.
trends.name: Garconne look

sources.quote: Likewise, Karina Reddy of the Fashion Institute of Technology pointed out: "Despite these departures from the prevailing mode of the previous decade, the popular styles of the early 1930s were similar in their simple lines to the popular garçonne look of the twenties.
Called garçonne in French ("boy" with a feminine suffix), flapper style made girls look young and boyish: short hair, flattened breasts, and straight waists accentuated it.
Corsets were declining in popularity, and the newly popular boyish look was typically achieved through the use of girdles and bust bodices.

trends.description: Thick glasses and nerdy clothes worn as fashion.
trends.name: Geek chic

sources.quote: Horn-rimmed glasses were also associated with the geek-chic trend.
American Apparel made normcore a prominent aspect of hipster culture in the US from 2016 onwards.

trends.name: Wrap dress

sources.quote: In 1942 her "Popover" dress debuted: a denim wrap dress that came with a matching oven mitt, sold by Lord & Taylor as "The Original Utility Fashion."
Von Fürstenberg's wrap dress design, essentially a robe, was among the most popular fashion styles of the 1970s for women and would also be credited as a symbol of women's liberation.
These classic ensembles of the 1960s and 1970s include tailored skirt suits, low heels, wrap dresses, shift dresses, silk or cotton blouses, and jewelry with a refined style.

trends.description: Shiny, futuristic, pink and rhinestoned pop-star style from around the year 2000.
trends.name: Y2K

sources.quote: Y2K fashion remained popular from the late 1990s until approximately 2022.
Y2K may also borrow elements from McBling aesthetic, which is sometimes conflated.
Y2K women's fashion from the late 1990s and 2000s became a major influence, especially among social media users.

trends.description: Stretchy flared or fitted workout trousers worn everywhere.
trends.name: Yoga pants

sources.quote: Yoga Pants and sports bras  remained popular in athleisure wardrobes for women, while men commonly wore 5-inch inseam athletic shorts and hoodies for comfort and mainstream style.
Characterized as "fashionable, dressed-up sweats and exercise clothing", athleisure grew during the mid-2010s, from the popularity of yoga pants that emerged throughout the mid to late 2000s.

Garments such as leggings, joggers, yoga pants, and athletic fabrics were no longer limited to fitness contexts, instead appearing in casual and even workplace settings, such as with the popularity of jeggings.

trends.description: Swing-loving Paris youth in oversized jackets during the occupation.
trends.name: Zazous

sources.quote: Among occupied Paris's most visible youth subcultures were the Zazous, enthusiasts of American swing music that the German occupiers had forbidden.

trends.description: A long, wide-shouldered jacket over high-waisted pegged trousers, worn by Black and Mexican American youth.
trends.name: Zoot suit

sources.quote: The most controversial men's fashion of the wartime period was the zoot suit.

Pachuco style Zoot suits, fedoras and panama hats made a comeback, together with more typical casual rockabilly fashions for everyday wear such as slim jeans, black leather jackets, bowling shirts, brightly colored blouses and flouncy skirts for girls, polka dot dresses with petticoats, and flowers worn in the hair.
